title: Adopt hybrid CAS with atomic slim-builder image migration
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Background: Our CI build times and bandwidth costs remain a major source of engineering churn. Many pipelines still re-download/ rebuild large language-specific toolchains and rebuild identical layers due to non-content-addressed artifacts and oversized builder images. Goal: Reduce median CI job wall time for core build pipelines by 30-50% and reduce public egress/storage costs by ~40% through a two-pronged approach: 1) Introduce a hybrid content-addressable cache (CAS) architecture that combines local BuildKit cache for fast warm caches with an S3-backed CAS proxy for cross-runner cache sharing. 2) Migrate to atomic, minimal 'slim-builder' images that separate base runtime from language-specific toolchains and lint runners to enable better layer reuse and smaller pull sizes.

Success metrics (target within first 8 weeks):
- Median CI build wall time reduction: >= 35% for frontend and backend monorepo builds
- Cold-cache job pull size reduction: >= 60% smaller builder image bytes
- Cache hit rate for tokenizable artifacts: >= 85% for repeated PRs
- Monthly egress/storage cost reduction target: 35-45%

Design decisions & approach:
- Hybrid CAS: run BuildKit/kaniko with a local disk-primed CAS for latency-sensitive runners, and push missing blobs to an S3-backed remote CAS (s3://redwood-ci-cas) via a proxy service. The proxy will sign/verify upload URLs and enforce TTL policies to bound storage growth.
- Atomic builder images: produce a small immutable base image (os/runtime + libc + minimal tooling) pinned per distro+arch and separate language toolchain layers as OCI artifacts that are pulled on-demand and cached in CAS. This avoids frequent invalidation of the large base image and keeps the builder image small enough for fast cold pulls.
- Deterministic build hashes: introduce a buildstamp manifest to compute content-addressed keys for produced artifacts and to enable safe cache lookups/invalidations across runners.
- Toolchain lint unbundling: move linters and heavy dev-only runtimes out of the default builder and provide them as a separate on-demand layer for pipeline stages that actually need linting.

Migration plan (phases):
1) Prototype (done): small cohort of CI runners (staging) with BuildKit remote cache + S3 CAS proxy. Measured prototype on 12 runs.
2) Stabilize (current): harden proxy auth, add TTL policy, integrate signed cache manifests, and publish a slim base image CVE scan.
3) Canary rollout: enable hybrid CAS for 10% CI runners and convert 2 high-volume jobs to slim-builder images with priming CI jobs to pre-populate CAS.
4) Full rollout: migrate remaining pipelines, retire legacy builder images and deprecated cache endpoints.

Testing and validation:
- Benchmark harness: run nightly 50-run bench for each critical pipeline comparing warm, prime, and cold conditions.
- Canary health checks: monitor build latency, cache hit ratio, cache upload success rate, and storage growth. Automatic rollback if failed uploads > 5% over 1 hour or median build time regresses beyond baseline.

Operational concerns & trade-offs:
- Complexity overhead: introducing CAS proxy and signing increases ops surface. Mitigation: simple API and clear runbooks; start with managed S3 lifecycle rules.
- Cache poisoning: use signed buildstamp manifests and prefix scoping to customer/service to prevent cross-tenant collisions.
- Security: ensure proxy runs in private VPC and uses short-lived credentials for runners.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ci/hybrid-cas-atomic-builders (internal)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1423
- Bench results (prototype): https://dash.redwood.ai/ci/bench/ENG-515001/prototype

Next steps (short-term):
- Address infra IAM blocker for CAS uploads (ENG-250007)
- Finalize SSL cert rotation for proxy endpoint
- Create priming jobs for the top 10 busiest repos to populate CAS before canary launch
